name: Folliculitis shower hygiene (post-gym shower)
lead: Showering soon after sweating is a hygiene habit that some people adopt to reduce body acne ("bacne") and folliculitis.[1][2]

Wikipedia describes folliculitis as inflammation of hair follicles, most often from Staphylococcus aureus, with friction from clothing, blocked follicles and shaving listed as triggers.[1] The article on acne mechanica lists heat, friction and pressure as causes and mentions showering soon after exercise as a suggestion, while noting that the page itself is flagged for needing better medical sources.[2]

paras: Practitioners shower after workouts to remove sweat and oil. General references list cleansers with salicylic acid or benzoyl peroxide as options, which may sting sensitive skin.[2]

Wikipedia states most simple folliculitis resolves on its own and treatments include topical antiseptics or antibiotics depending on type.[1] No controlled study of post-exercise showering for preventing folliculitis was found.

card.summary: Showering after sweat to limit body acne; suggested in general references, untested in trials.

quick.overview:
Some people shower soon after sweating to reduce body acne and folliculitis.

General references suggest it as a measure against acne mechanica, but no controlled study was found.
quick.mechanism: The practice aims to remove sweat, oil and surface bacteria that can irritate follicles.
quick.risks: No harms are described; over-washing or harsh cleansers can irritate skin per general advice.
